policyDecision.source: User clarification in this conversation, 2026-10-22; reconciles conflicting > signs on Blueprint p.1 with its Course 01/44 gates and existing adult pilot
policyDecision.appliesTo: proposed-next-release; existing draft-1 pilot policy remains unchanged

lessonAdditions.concept: Use AND, OR and NOT to compare two fictional true/false conditions; represent each result in a truth table and connect the conditions to simple logic-gate symbols. Introduce a single binary 0/1 signal as a representation, not a person's identity.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Using picture cards, blocks or a printed four-row grid, predict whether a simulated room light turns on when a switch AND a safety sensor are active; compare the OR and NOT alternatives.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: Correctly label every row for two input conditions and explain one AND/OR/NOT result orally, in text or through an accessible block trace.
lessonAdditions.safeguard: Use only fictional switches and simulated components; do not ask young learners to wire circuits.

lessonAdditions.concept: Trace a compound Boolean decision and distinguish the expression's predicted output from a guessed answer.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Complete a four-case decision table for a fictional quiz that accepts either a correct answer OR an approved retry, then test one changed input.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: All four outcomes agree with the declared Boolean rule, and the learner identifies a corrected error.

lessonAdditions.concept: Record repeatable steps and distinguish a syntax error from a logic error in a prepared visual/text example.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Run a prewritten fictional story, record input, expected output and actual output, and replay the failure before changing any step.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: A second learner can reproduce the failure from the report without being shown the answer.

lessonAdditions.concept: Bridge the existing block/pseudocode lesson to introductory Python print, a named variable and a fictional input, without assuming every learner has a personal device.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Translate a short, prewritten block sequence into Python statements in an embedded supervised editor; offer a printout/picture-card trace and oral explanation as an accessible practice path.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: The program or equivalent trace produces the expected greeting and the learner identifies the variable's role.
lessonAdditions.safeguard: Use fictional names only and never request a real student's identifying details.

lessonAdditions.concept: Connect client/server request-response to a safe, high-level network-connectivity diagram, distinguishing a disconnected client from an unavailable server.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Arrange browser, network, server and response cards for a fictional information site; identify which boundary is affected when a response does not arrive.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: The diagram places client and server correctly and explains one non-invasive connectivity check.

lessonAdditions.concept: Make the existing tags/elements/links outcome explicit: distinguish a link's readable text, href target and surrounding semantic element.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Create a local navigation link between two fictional HTML pages and inspect its keyboard focus and destination label.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: A keyboard user can activate the link and predict its destination from the visible text; no personal data is published.

lessonAdditions.concept: Explicitly distinguish String, Integer, Float and Boolean values, and choose an appropriate type for an entirely synthetic example.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Annotate four fictional values in a simple Python list/dictionary and explain why adding two numbers differs from concatenating text.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: Learner classifies all four types, predicts two outputs, and explains a mistaken conversion.

lessonAdditions.concept: Assess variable assignment, input/output, IF/ELIF/ELSE and finite WHILE/FOR loops rather than merely naming those constructs.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: In a synthetic budget or quiz, add a three-way decision and a bounded loop; trace a typical input, boundary case and invalid input.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: Independent tests exercise each branch and both loop paths; invalid input is handled without an uncontrolled loop.
lessonAdditions.safeguard: No real spending, grades, contacts or accounts in sample data.

lessonAdditions.concept: Extend data-quality discussion to how incomplete or unbalanced synthetic training examples could affect a model's results.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Compare counts in two fictional categories and describe which examples a hypothetical model rarely sees.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: Learner states one justified limitation and a fairer way to collect or represent examples, without claiming to have trained a real model.

lessonAdditions.concept: Explicitly identify a primary key, a foreign key and why an identifier should be unique in a fictional course-enrolment schema.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Mark the key columns on two toy tables, then predict which duplicate or missing reference a constraint would reject.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: The learner marks both keys correctly and explains one prevented inconsistent record.

lessonAdditions.concept: A website connects to a database through a server/API and access controls, not through browser-held database credentials.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Trace a request from a mock frontend through a mock server to a disposable dataset and back; identify where validation and authentication belong.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: Diagram separates browser, backend and fictional database; it includes no real personal record or exposed secret.

lessonAdditions.concept: Explain at a conceptual level how an algorithm uses training examples to detect patterns and why outputs are not automatically true.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Compare predictions from two tiny, invented training sets and identify which missing examples might change a prediction.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: Learner names a limitation of the examples and an independent way to check a claim; no live AI connection is required.

lessonAdditions.concept: Connect synthetic training-data imbalance to AI bias and human oversight; distinguish a model estimate from a decision about a person.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Review a fictional unequal dataset, describe a risk and write a human escalation or correction step.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: The artefact documents one plausible bias, a verification step and an explicit privacy boundary.

lessonAdditions.concept: Recognise the role of a router, access point and a safe conceptual IP/DNS configuration; keep changes in a fictional network diagram.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Label devices on a simulated small-office network and choose a safe route to troubleshoot a disconnected client.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: Diagram labels the boundaries and lists one check that does not touch a real school or neighbour's network.

lessonAdditions.concept: Recognise phishing, malware and repeated password-guessing (brute force) as threats; use only defensive descriptions, not attack instructions.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Sort fictional warning-sign cards and choose an approved reporting path for a suspicious login alert or message.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: All safety-critical scenarios choose a protective response and avoid interacting with a real target.
lessonAdditions.safeguard: No credential guessing, exploit labs, live scans or real phishing messages for learners.

lessonAdditions.concept: Connect password authentication, passphrases and MFA to the protection of fictional accounts; never collect a real password in a lesson.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Compare two imaginary sign-in safeguards and explain why reusing a password creates a risk.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: Learner recommends a suitable defensive control and identifies where to report unexpected login activity.

lessonAdditions.concept: Explain encryption in transit versus at rest at a high level, and why access control, backups and redundancy protect different things.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Label encrypted transport, restricted access and a recoverable backup on a fictional school-app diagram.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: Learner chooses an appropriate protective control for two scenarios and explains that encryption alone is not a backup.
lessonAdditions.safeguard: Conceptual protection only; do not imply this is a security qualification or expose production keys.

lessonAdditions.concept: Reuse the Course 09 AND/OR/NOT truth-table idea to express simulated sensor inputs, processing and outputs without requiring physical equipment.
lessonAdditions.guidedActivity: Describe a virtual light indicator that activates only when a fictional sensor AND an enable switch are on; compare its four input cases.
lessonAdditions.assessmentEvidence: The simulation or paper trace satisfies all four cases and the learner names a safe failure state.
lessonAdditions.safeguard: No mains electricity, real wiring or unsupervised hardware access.

toolPlacements.purpose: Optional picture-block sequencing for a learning routine; no new prerequisite
Reproduce and repair a block-program bug
Mock API responses without real network calls
Inspect training-data balance without live AI
